final_answer:
IN A FREE MARKET, THE INTERACTION OF SUPPLY AND DEMAND DETERMINES THE PRICE OF GOODS AND SERVICES. SUPPLIERS OFFER MORE AS PRICES INCREASE (SUPPLY CURVE SLOPES UPWARD), WHILE CONSUMERS BUY LESS AS PRICES RISE (DEMAND CURVE SLOPES DOWNWARD). THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE OCCURS WHERE THESE CURVES INTERSECT, BALANCING QUANTITY SUPPLIED AND DEMANDED. IF PRICES ARE ABOVE EQUILIBRIUM, A SURPLUS EMERGES; BELOW IT, A SHORTAGE OCCURS. MARKETS ADJUST THROUGH PRICE CHANGES TO REACH EQUILIBRIUM.

WHEN A GOVERNMENT IMPOSES A PRICE CEILING (A LEGAL MAXIMUM PRICE), IT RESTRICTS PRICES BELOW THE EQUILIBRIUM LEVEL. THIS CREATES A SHORTAGE, AS CONSUMERS DEMAND MORE THAN SUPPLIERS ARE WILLING TO PROVIDE AT THE LOWER PRICE. CONSEQUENCES INCLUDE LONG LINES, BLACK MARKETS, REDUCED QUALITY, AND INEFFICIENCY. SUPPLIERS MAY REDUCE PRODUCTION OR EXIT THE MARKET, HURTINg BOTH CONSUMERS (who face shortages) AND PRODUCERS (who earn less revenue). EXAMPLES INCLUDE RENT CONTROL OR PRICE FLOORS ON BASIC GOODS.
